value.description: Lumen & Loom Studio Ltd is a London-based textile design studio, founded in 2026 by Maya Chen, Oliver Grant and Priya Shah and based at a shared workshop in Hackney Wick, East London. We design and handweave sustainable home textiles (cushions, throws, table linen and wall hangings) from British wool, organic cotton and recycled yarns. Alongside our own collection we run small-group weaving workshops and take bespoke commissions for interior designers and boutique hotels.
value.mission: To bring slow, handmade craft back into everyday homes: making beautiful, durable textiles from responsibly sourced materials, paying fair prices along our supply chain, and teaching people the skills to make and repair for themselves.
value.positioning: For design-conscious Londoners and interior professionals who want homeware with a story, Lumen & Loom is an independent textile studio that makes every piece by hand in London from traceable, low-impact yarns. Unlike mass-market homeware brands, each piece is made in small batches, can be repaired for life, and comes with the name of the weaver who made it. Unlike other makers, we also open our studio: customers can learn to weave with us.
value.vision: By 2030, to be London's best-known independent weaving studio: a self-sustaining team of eight makers, a collection stocked by twenty UK independent retailers, a waiting list for our workshops, and a verified low-carbon supply chain from sheep to sofa.

value.philosophy: We believe the things we live with shape how we live. Fast, disposable homeware teaches us to replace rather than care; a well-made textile, repaired and kept for decades, teaches the opposite. Our work is a small, practical argument for slowness: fewer, better things, made close to home by people you can meet.
value.values:
1. Craft over speed
2. Honesty about materials and prices
3. Care for people and planet
4. Openness: share skills, not secrets
5. Community before scale
value.principles:
1. Every yarn we use is traceable to its farm or mill.
2. We pay our makers and suppliers a London Living Wage or better.
3. We repair anything we have made, for life.
4. We never discount to clear stock; we make to order instead.
5. We decide by consensus of the three founders on anything that affects people or materials.
value.manifesto: We stand for things made slowly and kept for a lifetime. We stand for knowing who made your cushion and where the wool came from. We stand against throwaway homeware, hidden supply chains and craft reduced to a style. Come and see how it's made. Better still, come and make it with us.

value.teamGaps: No one on the team has run e-commerce and digital marketing at scale, or managed textile production beyond our own looms.
value.teamCover: A freelance e-commerce specialist covers the online shop and digital marketing for the first year while Oliver completes a digital marketing course. A retired mill production manager mentors us on sourcing and small-batch production. Hale & Co Accountants and our lawyer cover year-end accounts and legal work, and we plan to hire and train an apprentice weaver to add studio production capacity.

value.aesthetics: A maker in their thirties in a well-worn oatmeal linen apron over undyed wool knitwear, sleeves pushed up. Natural fibres only, in cream, clay, moss green and indigo. Short nails, a little lanolin on the hands, a faint smell of wool and cedar. Always framed by the studio: north light through tall windows, looms in the background, spools of yarn on open shelves.
value.attitude-body-language: Relaxed and grounded. Stands side-on to you at the loom rather than across a counter, inviting you in. Slow, deliberate hand movements; hands often in frame, touching the cloth. Warm eye contact and an easy smile; comfortable with pauses. Never hurried, never selling.
value.communication-voice: Calm, mid-low pitch, unhurried pace. Speaks plainly and specifically, naming the farm, the yarn weight and the hours a piece took, and explains craft terms the first time they come up. Short sentences, British spelling, gentle humour, no hype words (no 'luxury', no 'curated'). Asks questions and listens.
value.imprint: First impression: 'these people really know what they're doing, and they're kind.' Lasting impression: a feeling of calm and of having learned something, and the urge to touch the cloth. People should leave wanting to keep what they buy for decades, and to come back and make something themselves.

segments.name: Conscious London Homemakers

description.demographics: Adults 28–55, mostly women (≈70%), household income £55k+, degree-educated, homeowners or long-term renters; many in creative, professional or public-sector jobs.
description.geographics: Greater London first, especially East and North London (Hackney, Islington, Walthamstow, Stoke Newington), then UK-wide online.
description.purchasing: Spend £400–1,500 a year on homeware; buy fewer, better pieces; research before buying; pay 20–40% more for sustainable, handmade and local; buy gifts at Christmas and for weddings.
description.market-size:
UK homeware market ≈ £13bn; UK soft furnishings ≈ £2.5bn. Roughly 450,000 London households fit the profile; a realistic reachable niche of ~15,000 buyers of premium handmade textiles.

Outlook: overall homeware spending is flat, but demand for sustainable, traceable and British-made products keeps growing; buyers increasingly discover makers on Instagram and buy direct online, and rising cotton and wool prices favour small-batch makers who can price on craft rather than volume.

profiles.name: The Considered Nester

description.personal: Hannah, 36, UX designer, lives with her partner in a Victorian flat in Stoke Newington; recently renovated; no children yet.
description.psychographics: Values craft, provenance and calm; anti-fast-fashion; enjoys slow weekends, markets and galleries; wants her home to feel personal, not catalogue-bought.
description.hubs: Instagram (interiors and makers), Pinterest, Broadway Market, Columbia Road, Crafts Council events, The Modern House journal, Apartamento.
description.habits: Discovers on Instagram and at markets; researches makers’ websites; buys online and at pop-ups; reads reviews; subscribes to a few newsletters.

profiles.goals: A home that feels warm, unique and made to last; owning things with a story; supporting local makers.
profiles.challenges: Mass-market textiles look generic and pill quickly; “sustainable” claims are hard to trust; handmade pieces are hard to find in person.
profiles.objections: Price compared with high-street cushions; delivery times for made-to-order; worries about care and washing.

social: Share a home that reflects her values

profiles.name: The Maker-Curious Gifter

description.personal: Tom, 42, secondary-school teacher in Walthamstow, two children; buys thoughtful gifts and looks for weekend activities with friends or his partner.
description.psychographics: Hands-on, curious, would rather do something than buy something; values experiences, learning and local community.
description.hubs: Time Out, Eventbrite, Instagram, local Facebook groups, Hackney Wick open studios, Walthamstow Garden Party.
description.habits: Books experiences online a few weeks ahead; buys gift vouchers; responds to “last places” emails; shops locally at Christmas.

profiles.goals: Give gifts that mean something; learn a real craft; spend screen-free time with people he cares about.
profiles.challenges: Generic gift ideas; craft classes that feel rushed or crowded; not knowing whether he will be any good at it.
profiles.objections: Class price per head; scheduling around children; travelling across London.

social: A shared experience with friends or partner

segments.valueProposition: For Londoners who want a calm, personal home without the throwaway cycle, Lumen & Loom makes handwoven cushions, throws and linens in Hackney from traceable British wool and organic cotton. Each piece is signed by its maker and repaired for life, and we teach you to weave your own. Unlike high-street and lifestyle brands, you know exactly who made it, where the yarn came from, and that it will last.

competitors.name: Independent weavers on Etsy & at craft markets

description.offerings: Handwoven cushions, scarves and wall hangings; one-off pieces, variable quality.
description.market: Craft-market shoppers and Etsy buyers UK-wide; similar values-driven customers.
description.acquisition: Etsy search, Instagram, weekend markets (Broadway Market, Spitalfields).
description.experience: Personal but inconsistent; slow replies; limited aftercare.

competitors.strengths: Authentic handmade story; low prices; large marketplace reach.
competitors.weaknesses: No brand consistency; few offer repair or traceability; tiny capacity.
competitors.opportunities: Most do not run workshops or sell to trade.
competitors.threats: Price undercutting; Etsy algorithm favours volume sellers.
competitors.insights: We compete on consistency, traceable materials, lifetime repair and the studio experience rather than on price.

competitors.name: Premium lifestyle homeware brands

description.offerings: Wool and linen throws and cushions, largely factory-made overseas (e.g. The White Company, Toast Home).
description.market: Affluent UK households; strong in London.
description.acquisition: Flagship stores, catalogues, paid social, large email lists.
description.experience: Polished and reliable; fast delivery; easy returns.

competitors.weaknesses: Not handmade; vague provenance; little personality.
competitors.threats: Frequent sales anchor customers to lower prices.
competitors.insights: Show the maker, the farm and the hours behind each piece; offer made-to-order colours they cannot.

competitors.name: High-street homeware (H&M Home, IKEA, Dunelm)

description.market: Mass market, all ages and incomes.
description.offerings: Buying cheap mass-produced cushions and throws and replacing them every year or two instead of investing in one handmade piece.

competitors.weaknesses: Short lifespan; environmental cost; no story.
competitors.opportunities: Customers upgrading from their first flat look for “grown-up” pieces.
competitors.threats: Trend cycles make handmade look expensive by comparison.
competitors.insights: Frame our pieces as a one-off investment with cost-per-year and repair for life.

segments.name: Interior Designers & Boutique Hospitality

description.business-data: Design studios of 1–15 people; boutique hotels of 10–60 rooms; restaurants and members’ clubs refurbishing every 5–7 years; many with B Corp or sustainability commitments.
description.demographics: Decision-makers aged 30–55: independent interior designers, studio founders and boutique-hotel owners or operations managers.
description.geographics: London first (Shoreditch, Clerkenwell, Marylebone design studios); then boutique hotels and restaurants across the South East and UK cities.
description.purchasing: Project budgets from £2k (single room) to £40k (hotel refurbishment) for soft furnishings; buy on specification with samples, lead times and trade pricing; repeat business when a supplier is reliable.
description.market-size:
Around 3,000 interior design practices in London and ~1,200 independent boutique hotels in the UK; target 30–50 trade relationships within five years.

Outlook: boutique hotels and restaurants are refurbishing again, with briefs asking for local craft and lower-impact materials; fire-safety rules for contract textiles (BS 5867 / BS 7176) mean fabrics must be tested and certified for commercial use.

profiles.name: The Sustainability-Led Interior Designer

description.personal: Amelia, 41, founder of a 6-person interior studio in Clerkenwell working on boutique hotels and high-end residential projects.
description.psychographics: Wants every project to tell a local, sustainable story; proud of working with makers; detail-obsessed and deadline-driven.
description.hubs: LinkedIn, Instagram, Clerkenwell Design Week, London Design Festival, Decorex, BIID membership, Dezeen.
description.habits: Sources through trade fairs, maker directories and recommendations; requests samples and spec sheets; orders via purchase order with 30-day terms.

profiles.goals: Distinctive, sustainable interiors that win clients and awards; reliable makers she can return to.
profiles.challenges: Small makers miss deadlines or cannot scale; poor documentation for fire regulations and sustainability reporting.
profiles.objections: Lead times, capacity for larger orders, fire-retardancy compliance for hospitality, trade pricing.

segments.valueProposition: For interior designers and boutique hotels who want a local, sustainable signature in every project, Lumen & Loom weaves bespoke textiles to specification in London, with samples in a week, fixed lead times and a documentation pack covering materials, carbon and fire compliance. Unlike contract mills, we make small runs and one-offs; unlike solo makers, we deliver on time.

competitors.name: Contract textile mills (e.g. Kvadrat, Designers Guild Contract)

description.offerings: Large contract fabric ranges, fire-rated, sold by the metre to the trade.
description.market: Hotels, offices and residential designers worldwide.
description.acquisition: Showrooms, sales reps, trade fairs, sample libraries.
description.experience: Professional, reliable, but impersonal and not bespoke at small scale.

competitors.weaknesses: Minimum orders; little story; limited bespoke work for small projects.
competitors.opportunities: Designers seeking a local, handmade signature piece alongside mill fabrics.
competitors.insights: Position as the handmade signature layer (cushions, throws, headboards and art textiles), not as a replacement for contract fabrics.

value.situation: Lumen & Loom Studio Ltd was incorporated in March 2026 by Maya Chen, Oliver Grant and Priya Shah and opens its Hackney Wick studio in October 2026. We sell a handwoven homeware collection online and at London markets, run beginner weaving workshops, and are starting bespoke commissions and a trade collection for interior designers and boutique hotels. Customers find us through Instagram, markets, word of mouth and design fairs. We are funded by £13,000 of founders’ capital, a £15,000 Start Up Loan and an £8,000 Hackney grant (half received). Monthly fixed costs are about £7,500, mostly three modest director salaries and rent; revenue starts small and is expected to cover costs from around August 2027. An angel round of £20,000 is in preparation to close a funding gap before then.

strengths: Three complementary founders: craft, sales and operations
Genuinely handmade in London with traceable British materials
Two revenue types: products and workshops
Lifetime repair service no competitor offers
weaknesses: Cash runway of only a few months without new funding
Heavy reliance on Maya for weaving and teaching
opportunities: Growing demand for sustainable, local interiors among designers and hotels
Experience gifting and craft workshops booming in London
Grant and SEIS-backed angel funding for creative businesses
threats: Rent review on the studio in 2028

value.compass: By 2030, Lumen & Loom is London’s best-known independent weaving studio: a team of eight makers, a collection stocked by twenty UK independents, commissions for boutique hotels across the UK, a workshop programme with a waiting list, and a fully traceable low-carbon supply chain. Profitable, and still making every piece by hand in Hackney.
